outcome: The conjecture (every even integer greater than 2 is the sum of two primes) remains open: no proof, disproof, or verified case-resolution has appeared since 26 January 2024. The strongest genuinely new result found in the window is an unrelated bound on Goldbach numbers in short intervals (a related problem, not a case of the stated conjecture), and every AI-adjacent item found is either non-credible, unmerged/unverified, or produced no mathematical content that changes the stated conjecture.
summary: The Goldbach conjecture (every even natural number > 2 is the sum of two primes) is untouched in the window 26 Jan 2024 - present: no proof, disproof, or settlement of any case was found. The conjecture is still verified computationally only up to 4×10^18 (a 2013-era bound; per §3.1, further verification would not count as progress on an existence/infinitude-type question in any case, and no extension of that bound was found or claimed). The closest thing to real mathematical progress found is Chirre & Hagen, 'On Goldbach Numbers in Short Intervals' (arXiv 2512.23534, a 2025-vintage preprint number under the 2512.* scheme), which assuming RH improves the constant for the shortest interval guaranteed to contain a Goldbach number from 9696 (Cully-Hugill & Dudek) to 123. This is a genuine, human-authored, non-AI advance, but it is about a different, related question (existence of a Goldbach number in a short interval, conditional on RH) rather than a case of the stated conjecture itself, so per §3.1 it does not change this bullet's status and is recorded here only for completeness — it does not count as `progress` on this record. On the AI side, three lines of 'evidence' were checked and all rejected: (1) an article ('GPT-6 Astra Unveils Major Breakthrough...', 36kr.com) claiming an AI model proved a 'weak Liouville form' of Goldbach; the article itself carries a publication date of 21 September 2026 in the future relative to when it was retrieved, cites no verifiable arXiv or Lean artifact, and reads as speculative/fabricated content, not a real result — discarded entirely. (2) A GitHub issue (#3952, opened 6 May 2026 by an outside contributor 'Suro-One') titled 'Erdős Problem 242 (Erdős-Straus) and Goldbach Conjecture resolved', linking to a personal repository (Suro-One/auro-zera_Erdos-Straus_proof) containing a file 'GoldbachZera.lean'. This is an unsolicited, unmerged, unreviewed external submission to DeepMind's formal-conjectures issue tracker; nothing indicates it was accepted, verified, or endorsed by DeepMind or any mathematician, and the repository's own open/closed status pattern (multiple other issues flag 'status mismatch' between the repo and problem-tracking sites) gives no indication Goldbach's status was ever changed to solved. Under §6.1 an unreviewed claim by an unknown party is not even `claimed`-worthy without further corroboration, and no corroboration exists — treated as noise. (3) A ScienceDirect article ('Bridging Mathematics and AI: A novel approach to Goldbach's Conjecture') and a dev.to post describing an 'AI research engine' finding a Chebyshev-bias-like pattern in Goldbach data are exploratory/heuristic studies using LLMs or search tools to look for patterns in already-verified computational data; neither produces a proof, a case-resolution, or a bound on the open conjecture, so under §6.2 they are `ai_role: none` even if they existed at the level of a 'finding' (which they do not, at the level of this conjecture). Overall: no status change, no credible AI involvement of any kind that touches the stated conjecture.
competing_reading: If the DeepMind formal-conjectures issue #3952 (or the underlying Lean file) turned out to compile without `sorry` and were independently confirmed as a sound proof, this record would need to move to `claimed` or higher with `ai_role` depending on how the proof was produced. This was not verified: the Lean file's contents could not be inspected in enough detail (10,000+ lines, page renders as GitHub metadata only) to rule out that it compiles, though an unsolicited, unmerged, unreviewed submission of this kind — bearing all the hallmarks of the many uncredited crank 'proofs' the triage record already flagged (ResearchGate, preprints.org, academia.edu, vixra) — is exactly the pattern the triage was right to dismiss.
what_would_settle_it: Independent compilation of Suro-One's GoldbachZera.lean against a trusted mathlib/Lean toolchain (checking for `sorry`, unsound axioms, or a mismatch between the formalized statement and the actual Goldbach conjecture), and/or any acknowledgement from DeepMind, a number theorist, or a math-news outlet that the issue was taken seriously rather than closed/ignored as spam.
